# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents main @cee599626b0ee12111dc8fb27ece83daebd9ae6e — ships:
    # #579 (conflict-rework: PR-anchored dispatch when no OPEN linked
    # issue — DIRTY machines PRs no longer dead-letter on closed issues),
    # #577/#578 (mutexExcludeSelf by fact of holding: a self-holding
    # candidate IS the holder — two approved ai_validating arms no longer
    # block each other into a total queue freeze; live fa #1068+#1088
    # 2026-09-30, ~40 min deadlock), #576 (review-machine-unlinked: a
    # MACHINE-authored validated PR with no OPEN linked issue gets its
    # one-time review — fixes the validated-forever starvation, live fa
    # #1068 19h / #1071 / #1075), #573 (every pack release is a
    # self-contained snapshot), #574 (DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY passed into
    # the agent run env), #572 (review-stale-verdict-unchecked: a
    # validated+reviewed PR whose head lost its checks gets a re-REVIEW
    # first; final validation stays in validate-armed), #571 (factory
    # teammate leg self-heals a broken dmtools install), #570 (SM
    # workflow budget 1 -> 3), #569 (rework: a fatal CLI failure is no
    # longer announced as "Rework Complete"),
    # #568 (mergeBot workspace/repository args), #566 (pack-registry
    # runner overrides).
    # Flip in lockstep with ai-teammate.yml — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@cee599626b0ee12111dc8fb27ece83daebd9ae6e
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: cee599626b0ee12111dc8fb27ece83daebd9ae6e
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

blocks.text:
# SM kicker factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# A tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost) ported from
# flutter_agent_harness `.github/workflows/sm-kicker.yml` so every machine
# repo gets it from the pack instead of keeping a drifting local copy.
#
# Why it exists: machine repos run dispatch-only CI (ci.yml `on.push` fires
# nothing on PR heads) and the Machine SM is the sole trigger. Two gaps
# leave a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick
#      and die.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet the
#      strict `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on
#      the new head SHA. The SM's validate-fresh/armed rules don't count
#      a no-code rebase as "validation due", so the contexts never appear.
#      Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents, 0 files
#      vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check contexts
#      NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on that head.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).
#
# Caller stub (flutter_agent_harness example):
#   name: SM kicker
#   on:
#     push: {branches-ignore: [main]}
#     schedule: [{cron: '13,43 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch:
#   permissions: {actions: write, contents: read, pull-requests: read, checks: read}
#   concurrency:
#     # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911, 2026-09-25):
#     # a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker for every
#     # other branch, stamping CANCELLED check-runs on random heads. The
#     # kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let them queue.
#     group: sm-kicker
#     cancel-in-progress: false
#   jobs:
#     kicker:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml            # this repo's SM stub name
#         ciWorkflow: ci.yml                    # this repo's CI entrypoint
#         requiredContexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
#       secrets:
#         githubToken: ${{ github.token }}
#   # epam/dmtools-dart example overrides:
#   #   smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml, ciWorkflow: quality.yml
#   #   requiredContexts: 'agents-suite,static,gate'
#
# Concurrency note: the group lives in the CALLER's job definition (GitHub
# attaches job-level concurrency to the reusable job) — keep the
# no-cancel-in-progress discipline from fa #911 there.

name: 'Factory · SM kicker'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label for the watchdog jobs (seconds-cheap; hosted is fine)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      smWorkflow:
        description: "File name of this repo's Machine SM stub to liveness-kick"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ciWorkflow:
        description: "File name of this repo's CI entrypoint to dispatch on codeless heads"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      requiredContexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check-run names guarding PR mergeability'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
      graceSeconds:
        description: 'Re-check window before dispatching CI (a dispatch may be in flight from the SM chain)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '45'
    secrets:
      githubToken:
        description: "Caller's token (github.token suffices: reads + same-repo workflow dispatch)"

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.githubToken }}
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            gh workflow run "${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.githubToken }}
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          req='${{ inputs.requiredContexts }}'
          ci_wf='${{ inputs.ciWorkflow }}'
          grace='${{ inputs.graceSeconds }}'
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\" and (.status == \"in_progress\" or .status == \"queued\" or .status == \"waiting\" or .status == \"pending\"))] | length")
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '[.check_runs[].name] | join("\n")' | grep -Fxc -f <(printf '%s\n' "${req//,//$'\n'}") || true)
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep "$grace"
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\")] | length")
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run "$ci_wf" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

Excellent — the factory workflow is fetched. Critical contract analysis:

**1. BLOCKING BUG in the factory port (and thus in this PR's "no behavior change" claim): the sm-liveness leg lost `-f dryRun=false`!**

The old local code:
```
gh workflow run machine-sm.yml -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -f dryRun=false
```
with the comment: "dryRun input defaults to TRUE: without the explicit flag the rescue tick logs its plan and performs no action (live: 2026-09-29 21:14/21:22/21:24 — kicker-dispatched ticks all ran dryRun: true and the SM stayed idle through a missed cron)."

The factory version (now executing):
```
gh workflow run "${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
```
NO `-f dryRun=false`. Per machine-sm.yml, `dryRun` input defaults to true → the rescue tick will run in DRY mode and perform no action. This is EXACTLY the live incident from 2026-09-29 (fa #1092), guarded by test/machine_kit/sm_kicker_test.dart. So the shared factory reintroduced the #1092 bug into the kicker's rescue leg. The sm-liveness leg becomes a no-op for its entire purpose: "SM idle → dispatch one tick" will dispatch a dry tick that does nothing, and the SM stays idle forever. That's a BLOCKING correctness regression — the whole reason the kicker exists (gap 1) is silently broken.

Wait — let me double-check machine-sm.yml's dryRun default: "workflow_dispatch inputs.dryRun default: true" — yes: `default: true`. And sm_kicker_test asserts that default stays true. So `gh workflow run machine-sm.yml` without `-f dryRun=` → dry run → "logs its plan and performs no action". Confirmed BLOCKING.

And the repo's own regression test (sm_kicker_test.dart) FAILS on this PR — CI red — which is exactly the guard doing its job. So BLOCKING #1: CI break (2 failing tests in sm_kicker_test.dart) + the underlying behavior regression the guards were written for: the factory kicker's rescue tick dispatches without `-f dryRun=false`, re-introducing the #1092 incident through the shared pack. The PR description claims "Без изменений в поведении" — false for the sm-liveness leg.

**2. `requiredContexts` check changed behavior — grep -Fxc -f <(printf...)`**:

Old local:
```
--jq '[.check_runs[].name | select(. == "Quality gate" or . == "JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" or . == "Binaries smoke gate")] | length'
```
New factory:
```
--jq '[.check_runs[].name] | join("\n")' | grep -Fxc -f <(printf '%s\n' "${req//,//$'\n'}") || true
```
Hmm: `${req//,//$'\n'}` — this replaces `,` with a literal `\n`?? In bash, `${var//pattern/replacement}` with replacement `$'\n'`... the replacement is the expansion of `$'\n'`? Actually inside parameter expansion, the replacement string undergoes expansion, so `${req//,/$'\n'}` — you write `"${req//,//$'\n'}"`. Wait, the syntax `${req//,//$'\n'}` — the first `/` after `req` means replace-all, pattern is `, then `//` ... hmm, `${req//,/REPL}` is the correct form: `${req//,/ Replacement}`. Writing `${req//,//$'\n'}` means pattern=`,` and replacement=`/$'\n'`?? No wait: `${req//pattern/string}`. Here after `//` the pattern is `,` (up to the next unescaped `/`), and the replacement is everything after that single separating `/`, which is `$'\n'`. The text is `//,//$'\n'`: `//` + pattern `,` + `/` separator + replacement `$'\n'`. So replacement = `$'\n'` (a literal newline). Good: turns "A,B,C" into "A\nB\nC". printf '%s\n' each line → "A\nB\nC\n". grep -Fxc -f <file> counts lines exactly matching any pattern (fixed strings). So found = number of check-run names matching one of the required contexts. Behavior equivalent to the old select count? Old: counts check runs whose name equals one of the three (each occurrence). New: grep -c counts matching LINES — same count. One subtle difference: grep -f with -x and fixed patterns; `grep -Fxc -f` — order of flags fine. `|| true` guards grep's exit 1 (no matches → found=""). But `found=$(... | grep ... || true)` → when no matches, grep outputs nothing, exit 1, `|| true` → found="" → `${found:-0}` → 0. OK equivalent.

Edge: process substitution `<(...)` requires bash — GitHub Actions default shell for run is bash (with `set -e`... actually default is `bash -e`). Fine on ubuntu. OK.

**3. The CI-active check changed subtly**: old checked `.name == "CI"`; new: `.name == \"$ci_wf\"` — ciWorkflow input is `ci.yml`, so it compares run name == "ci.yml". GitHub run `.name` is the workflow's `name:` field ("CI" presumably from ci.yml's name field) NOT the file name! The old code matched `.name == "CI"` — the human-readable workflow name. The new code compares against `ci.yml` (the file name). Workflow run objects from `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs` have `name` = the workflow run's name — which is the workflow `name:` attribute (e.g. "CI"), and ALSO `path` = ".github/workflows/ci.yml". So `.name == "ci.yml"` will NEVER match → the "CI already active" skip never triggers → head-completeness dispatches CI on codeless heads even when CI is already running, and the grace re-check (`ci > 0`) never sees CI → duplicate CI dispatches. That's a behavior change / bug in the factory (not the stub), but the stub passes `ciWorkflow: ci.yml` believing it's equivalent. Hmm wait — actually for workflow runs triggered via workflow_dispatch, `.name` is the display name ("CI"). Actually, careful: `workflow_runs[].name` — documented as "The name of the workflow run" — in practice it's the workflow's name (display name). So comparing to "ci.yml" fails. UNLESS ci.yml has no `name:` field, in which case GitHub displays the file path... Let me check ci.yml's name field in this repo.

Let me check: head -5 of .github/workflows/ci.yml.

If ci.yml has `name: CI`, then `.name == "ci.yml"` never matches → skip logic broken → duplicate dispatches (extra CI runs on codeless heads; each new kicker run re-dispatches CI — the grace window re-check also broken). Severity: IMPORTANT-to-BLOCKING (behavior regression vs. "no behavior change" claim; causes redundant CI runs, potential loops every 30 min: codeless head with zero required contexts gets CI dispatched every schedule tick if contexts don't appear... but once CI runs and stamps the three contexts, found > 0 → skip. So duplicates only while CI is in flight or if contexts never appear (e.g., CI fails before stamping). The grace re-check exists precisely to avoid double-dispatch while CI is launching; broken → double dispatch on consecutive ticks (13/43 cron = 30 min apart; push events too). Moderate impact, real regression vs old behavior.

Let me verify ci.yml name.

**4. The sm-liveness "active" check uses inputs.smWorkflow for the runs query** — fine: runs?workflow=machine-sm.yml works with file name. OK.

**5. Token passing**: factory declares `secrets.githubToken` and the stub maps `githubToken: ${{ github.token }}`. The machine-sm.yml comment warns: "github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead."

Hmm — that's a strong claim from a live bisect. If true in general, then in the new stub the factory's `secrets.githubToken` would be EMPTY → both kicker legs fail (`gh api` 401s) → the kicker stops working entirely (worse than dryRun bug — no rescue, no head-completeness). Is that GitHub behavior real? Actually, known GitHub quirk: when you explicitly map `github.token` in a reusable workflow `secrets:` block... I recall that `secrets: inherit` DOES pass github.token. For explicit mapping `FOO: ${{ github.token }}` — the docs say github.token is available in the `secrets` mapping of a reusable workflow call? There are community reports both ways; some say explicit mapping of github.token to reusable workflow secrets works fine. But THIS repo's machine-sm.yml records a live-verified case where it arrived empty. That live case may have been specific to that factory (e.g., job-level env in the factory evaluated before secrets propagation?? unlikely) org settings. I can't re-verify here; but the repo's OWN documented convention says explicit `${{ github.token }}` through a reusable call's secrets arrives empty, and the established pattern (machine-sm) routes…
The factory contract is now verifiable. Let me check one critical detail — how CI's workflow run name compares to what the factory matches:

Confirmed: `ci.yml` has `name: CI` (line 10). The factory's head-completeness leg queries:

```
--jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\" and ...)]"
```

with `ci_wf='ci.yml'` → `.name == "ci.yml"`. But workflow runs report `.name` = the workflow's display name = "CI" (that's why the OLD local code matched `.name == "CI"`). So:
- "CI already active on $sha — skip" NEVER matches → skips nothing.
- The grace-window re-check (`select(.name == \"ci.yml\")`) also never matches → "CI appeared during grace window" never triggers.

Consequence: on every kicker tick (cron 13,43 + every push on any PR branch), for every open-PR codeless merge head with zero required contexts, the factory dispatches a fresh `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref b` even when CI is already queued/running on that head, and the 45s grace dedup is dead. Multiple redundant CI dispatches (queue pressure, duplicated runs; on this repo CI is heavy). This is a real behavior regression vs. the "no behavior change" claim — BLOCKING? The dispatches are deduped later by the required-contexts check once CI stamps contexts; but during a CI run (~many minutes), consecutive ticks at 13/43 + pushes would re-dispatch. On push-heavy repos that's dozens of duplicate CI runs. I rate it BLOCKING (bug introduced via the pack; the stub's `ciWorkflow: ci.yml` input feeds the broken comparison — fix belongs in the factory: match `--jq "select(.path == \".github/workflows/$ci_wf\")"` or `.name == \"CI\"`; the stub can't fix it, but merge should be blocked until pack #586 lands and pin flips). Hmm — severity: it does cause duplicate CI dispatches — real bug, wastes runners, and pollutes. Since the review is of THIS repo's PR, and the fix must happen in dmtools-agents (or by not merging until fixed), BLOCKING is fair. Actually, let me double check `workflow_runs[].name` semantics: For workflow runs, `name` is "The name of the workflow run" — in practice the workflow's name (e.g., "CI"); if the run was triggered by a reusable workflow call... For runs of ci.yml itself, name = "CI". Also note: if the workflow file has a `name:`, GitHub's run `.name` is that name. Yes, old code (written from live behavior) used "CI". Confirmed mismatch.

Wait, one more consideration: could `.name` return "ci.yml" when the workflow has no name? Not the case here (name: CI exists). Good.

Now the sm-liveness leg — the factory dispatches `gh workflow run "${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"` WITHOUT `-f dryRun=false`. machine-sm.yml's dryRun input defaults to true (asserted by sm_kicker_test test 1). So the rescue tick always dispatches a DRY tick → SM stays idle → gap 1 uncovered. This re-introduces the exact #1092 incident (live 2026-09-29). BLOCKING — the kicker's primary purpose (rescue an idle SM) silently no-ops. And the repo's regression tests fail (CI red), which is the objective blocker: `dart test/machine_kit/sm_kicker_test.dart` → 2 failures.

Note: the factory's caller-example comment shows the stub without graceSeconds (optional input default '45') — the stub passing graceSeconds: '45' is harmless (explicit). Fine.

Now, is there any chance machine-sm.yml's dryRun default will change? sm_kicker_test pins default true. So no.

Token-secret question: machine-sm.yml NOTE claims github.token mapped through reusable-call secrets arrives empty (live-verified). If that generalizes, factory-sm-kicker's githubToken would be empty → `gh api` 401 → both legs fail every tick. But wait — is that plausible? GitHub docs (Reusing workflows): " secrets.<secret_id> ... Note: secrets: inherit ... secrets context is available". Known quirk reports: mapping `${{ github.token }}` explicitly DOES work in most cases... There are GitHub community threads where explicit `${{ github.token }}` in a reusable workflow's secrets block arrives empty when the workflow also uses `permissions` restrictions? I can't resolve from here. The repo's own record says it failed live once. The new factory explicitly documents `githubToken: "Caller's token (github.token suffices...)"` and the dmtools-agents#585 presumably tested it (the factory's own example shows exactly this mapping). The 01a45d24 factory header example literally shows `githubToken: ${{ github.token }}` — so the pack author believes it works. Given the conflicting live record in THIS repo (machine-sm), I'll flag as IMPORTANT: verify on first scheduled run / consider aligning with the machine-sm approach; at minimum record evidence in the PR. Actually — hold on. Let me re-read the machine-sm note: "github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead." Hmm, that's specifically about factory-sm.yml's SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN required-secret validation: "mapping a secret the callee does not declare is rejected" — the probe H2 comments. The empty-token claim is separate. There is a REAL known GitHub behavior: in a reusable workflow call, the `secrets` mapping DOES accept `${{ github.token }}` and delivers it — EXCEPT when... hmm, actually I recall: for `workflow_call`, secrets passed as `${{ github.token }}` DO get delivered (the callee sees the caller's token). The machine-sm live failure might have been caused by org policy or by the fact that `permissions` at caller top-level... Can't adjudicate. IMPORTANT with "verify live" recommendation.

Now the lockstep/guard-test findings:

A. sm_kicker_test.dart NOT updated → 2 CI test failures (BLOCKING, confirmed locally).
B. factory_stub_ref_test.dart stubs map not extended with sm-kicker.yml — violates the file's own "New stubs MUST be added here" rule; kicker escapes lockstep/echo/secrets guards (IMPORTANT).
C. Pin skew: kicker @01a45d24 vs SM/teammate/merge @cee5996 — the kicker dispatches ticks consumed by an OLDER factory snapshot; #580-#584 fixes ride only the kicker's snapshot. The stated repo invariant (same-ref lockstep) is broken silently (the guard doesn't cover the kicker — the two combine). IMPORTANT (recommend flipping the other three stubs to 01a45d24 in the same wave, or documenting why the split-pin is safe + adding the kicker to the guard map).

D. Token via secrets vs repo's documented live-verified quirk (IMPORTANT).
E. dryRun regression lives in the PACK (factory-sm-kicker.yml missing -f dryRun=false) — the stub PR claims "Без изменений в поведении" which is false; the fix must land in dmtools-agents (pass a new input e.g. smDispatchInputs or hardcode `-f dryRun=false`; better: factory should accept `smDispatchExtraArgs`/`smLiveTick` input) and the pin flipped. BLOCKING (same finding as A's root cause but worth a separate comment: the CI-red is the symptom; the root cause is the pack's lost flag → the #1092 incident returns).

Also the `.name == ci_wf` bug (BLOCKING-ish, IMPORTANT-to-BLOCKING). I'll mark it BLOCKING too? Let me think about severity discipline: "BLOCKING — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed." Duplicate CI dispatches = bug (resource waste, but also: for codeless merge heads with zero contexts, dispatching CI while CI is already running is harmless-ish except waste; plus the grace re-check dead). It IS a behavior change violating the PR's core claim. I'll classify as IMPORTANT actually... Hmm. The dryRun one is clearly BLOCKING (feature dead + CI red). The name-match one: head-completeness still functions (dispatches CI when contexts missing; the skip logic just under-skips). Effect: duplicate CI runs; each run on a codeless head eventually stamps the three contexts (or fails). The duplicated dispatch also races: two CI runs on the same head → both stamp contexts → benign but wasteful; required-check protection accepts first-completed. I'd rate IMPORTANT (not a correctness break of the protection, but real waste + a regression vs claimed parity). Hmm, but "merge would cause a bug" — duplicate dispatches ARE a bug (unintended behavior). But relative severity: moderate. I'll mark IMPORTANT with a note it must be fixed in the pack before/shortly after merge... Per guidance "When in doubt, start one level higher" → BLOCKING…

> NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.

If the quirk reproduces here, **both** kicker legs 401 on every tick — the watchdog dies silently (no SM rescue, no CI on codeless heads, PRs stuck with zero required contexts) and nothing in the stub surfaces the failure.

The pack's header example does show this exact mapping (dmtools-agents #585 presumably tested it), so the two repos' live evidence currently disagrees. Before merge, please:

Two related problems:

The kicker now executes pack code that includes #577–#584, while the SM leg it dispatches still runs `cee5996` — any loop fix in #580–#584 that spans kicker↔SM behavior is half-applied, silently. blocks.text:
# SM kicker factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# A tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost) ported from
# flutter_agent_harness `.github/workflows/sm-kicker.yml` so every machine
# repo gets it from the pack instead of keeping a drifting local copy.
#
# Why it exists: machine repos run dispatch-only CI (ci.yml `on.push` fires
# nothing on PR heads) and the Machine SM is the sole trigger. Two gaps
# leave a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick
#      and die.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet the
#      strict `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on
#      the new head SHA. The SM's validate-fresh/armed rules don't count
#      a no-code rebase as "validation due", so the contexts never appear.
#      Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents, 0 files
#      vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check contexts
#      NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on that head.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).
#
# Caller stub (flutter_agent_harness example):
#   name: SM kicker
#   on:
#     push: {branches-ignore: [main]}
#     schedule: [{cron: '13,43 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch:
#   permissions: {actions: write, contents: read, pull-requests: read, checks: read}
#   concurrency:
#     # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911, 2026-09-25):
#     # a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker for every
#     # other branch, stamping CANCELLED check-runs on random heads. The
#     # kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let them queue.
#     group: sm-kicker
#     cancel-in-progress: false
#   jobs:
#     kicker:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml            # this repo's SM stub name
#         ciWorkflow: ci.yml                    # this repo's CI entrypoint
#         requiredContexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
#   # No secrets needed: the kicker reads github.token directly (it resolves
#   # to the CALLER's token inside a reusable workflow).
#   # epam/dmtools-dart example overrides:
#   #   smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml, ciWorkflow: quality.yml
#   #   requiredContexts: 'agents-suite,static,gate'
#
# Concurrency note: the group lives in the CALLER's job definition (GitHub
# attaches job-level concurrency to the reusable job) — keep the
# no-cancel-in-progress discipline from fa #911 there.

name: 'Factory · SM kicker'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label for the watchdog jobs (seconds-cheap; hosted is fine)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      smWorkflow:
        description: "File name of this repo's Machine SM stub to liveness-kick"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ciWorkflow:
        description: "File name of this repo's CI entrypoint to dispatch on codeless heads"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      requiredContexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check-run names guarding PR mergeability'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
      graceSeconds:
        description: 'Re-check window before dispatching CI (a dispatch may be in flight from the SM chain)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '45'
    secrets: {}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    env:
      # github.token resolves to the CALLER's token inside a reusable
      # workflow — no secret plumbing needed for reads + same-repo dispatch.
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            # dryRun=false is LOAD-BEARING: the SM stub's workflow_dispatch
            # input defaults to true, and a flagless dispatch silently no-ops
            # (live incident 2026-09-29 21:14-21:24Z, fa guard #1092).
            gh workflow run "${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -f dryRun=false
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    env:
      # github.token resolves to the CALLER's token inside a reusable
      # workflow — no secret plumbing needed for reads + same-repo dispatch.
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          req='${{ inputs.requiredContexts }}'
          ci_wf='${{ inputs.ciWorkflow }}'
          grace='${{ inputs.graceSeconds }}'
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\" and (.status == \"in_progress\" or .status == \"queued\" or .status == \"waiting\" or .status == \"pending\"))] | length")
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '[.check_runs[].name] | join("\n")' | grep -Fxc -f <(printf '%s\n' "${req//,//$'\n'}") || true)
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep "$grace"
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\")] | length")
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run "$ci_wf" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

with `ci_wf='ci.yml'`. GitHub's `workflow_runs[].name` is the workflow's **display name** — `ci.yml` declares `name: CI` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:10`), so `.name` is `"CI"`, never `"ci.yml"`. The pre-port local code matched `.name == "CI"` for exactly this reason.

**Fix path** (pack-side, then flip this pin): match on `.path == ".github/workflows/$ci_wf"` — stable, no extra input needed — or accept the display name as a second input. Optionally add a pack-side regression guard so the next port can't reintroduce it (the #1092 pattern).

# SM kicker — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml
# (this repo carries only triggers + concurrency + this call — no logic to drift).
# Ported from the previous local copy (fa history: two-job watchdog,
# #911 concurrency diagnosis).
#
# Why it exists: this repo's CI is dispatch-only (ci.yml `on.push` fires
# nothing on PR heads) and the Machine SM is the sole trigger:
#   1. sm-liveness — SM idle → dispatch one tick;
#   2. head-completeness — codeless merge heads (2 parents, 0 files) with
#      zero required contexts get a CI dispatch (strict up-to-date).
#
# Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents main @01a45d24a071536a9f39603c2571f2e10f84a0b1 — ships the kicker
# together with the #577-#584 loop fixes (lockstep with machine-sm /
# machine-merge / ai-teammate stubs' pin wave).

name: SM kicker

run-name: 🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: machine-sm.yml / ci.yml
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911 diagnosis, 2026-09-25):
  # a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker for every
  # other branch, leaving sm-liveness/head-completeness check-runs stamped
  # CANCELLED on random heads ("Cancelled after 6s") and polluting PR
  # check rolls repo-wide. The kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs —
  # let them queue instead of cancelling; a bounded backlog is harmless.
  group: sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@01a45d24a071536a9f39603c2571f2e10f84a0b1
    with:
      smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml
      ciWorkflow: ci.yml
      requiredContexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
      graceSeconds: '45'
    secrets:
      githubToken: ${{ github.token }}

2. Look at the other factory stubs (machine-sm.yml, machine-merge.yml, ai-teammate.yml) to compare conventions — especially how they pass secrets and pin SHAs.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

But it's a big file. Let me focus on what matters for this review: the workflow file conventions. Let me look at other factory stubs to compare conventions (machine-sm.yml, machine-merge.yml, ai-teammate.yml).

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents main @cee599626b0ee12111dc8fb27ece83daebd9ae6e — ships:
    # #579 (conflict-rework: PR-anchored dispatch when no OPEN linked
    # issue — DIRTY machines PRs no longer dead-letter on closed issues),
    # #577/#578 (mutexExcludeSelf by fact of holding: a self-holding
    # candidate IS the holder — two approved ai_validating arms no longer
    # block each other into a total queue freeze; live fa #1068+#1088
    # 2026-09-30, ~40 min deadlock), #576 (review-machine-unlinked: a
    # MACHINE-authored validated PR with no OPEN linked issue gets its
    # one-time review — fixes the validated-forever starvation, live fa
    # #1068 19h / #1071 / #1075), #573 (every pack release is a
    # self-contained snapshot), #574 (DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY passed into
    # the agent run env), #572 (review-stale-verdict-unchecked: a
    # validated+reviewed PR whose head lost its checks gets a re-REVIEW
    # first; final validation stays in validate-armed), #571 (factory
    # teammate leg self-heals a broken dmtools install), #570 (SM
    # workflow budget 1 -> 3), #569 (rework: a fatal CLI failure is no
    # longer announced as "Rework Complete"),
    # #568 (mergeBot workspace/repository args), #566 (pack-registry
    # runner overrides).

# Why it exists: machine repos run dispatch-only CI (ci.yml `on.push` fires
# nothing on PR heads) and the Machine SM is the sole trigger. Two gaps
# leave a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick
#      and die.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet the
#      strict `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on
#      the new head SHA. The SM's validate-fresh/armed rules don't count
#      a no-code rebase as "validation due", so the contexts never appear.
#      Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents, 0 files
#      vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check contexts
#      NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on that head.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).
#
# Caller stub (flutter_agent_harness example):
#   name: SM kicker
#   on:
#     push: {branches-ignore: [main]}
#     schedule: [{cron: '13,43 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch:
#   permissions: {actions: write, contents: read, pull-requests: read, checks: read}
#   concurrency:
#     # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911, 2026-09-25):
#     # a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker for every
#     # other branch, stamping CANCELLED check-runs on random heads. The
#     # kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let them queue.
#     group: sm-kicker
#     cancel-in-progress: false
#   jobs:
#     kicker:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml            # this repo's SM stub name
#         ciWorkflow: ci.yml                    # this repo's CI entrypoint
#         requiredContexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
#       secrets:
#         githubToken: ${{ github.token }}
#   # epam/dmtools-dart example overrides:
#   #   smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml, ciWorkflow: quality.yml
#   #   requiredContexts: 'agents-suite,static,gate'
#
# Concurrency note: the group lives in the CALLER's job definition (GitHub
# attaches job-level concurrency to the reusable job) — keep the
# no-cancel-in-progress discipline from fa #911 there.

name: 'Factory · SM kicker'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label for the watchdog jobs (seconds-cheap; hosted is fine)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      smWorkflow:
        description: "File name of this repo's Machine SM stub to liveness-kick"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ciWorkflow:
        description: "File name of this repo's CI entrypoint to dispatch on codeless heads"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      requiredContexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check-run names guarding PR mergeability'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
      graceSeconds:
        description: 'Re-check window before dispatching CI (a dispatch may be in flight from the SM chain)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '45'
    secrets:
      githubToken:
        description: "Caller's token (github.token suffices: reads + same-repo workflow dispatch)"

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.githubToken }}
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            gh workflow run "${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.githubToken }}
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          req='${{ inputs.requiredContexts }}'
          ci_wf='${{ inputs.ciWorkflow }}'
          grace='${{ inputs.graceSeconds }}'
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\" and (.status == \"in_progress\" or .status == \"queued\" or .status == \"waiting\" or .status == \"pending\"))] | length")
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '[.check_runs[].name] | join("\n")' | grep -Fxc -f <(printf '%s\n' "${req//,//$'\n'}") || true)
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep "$grace"
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\")] | length")
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run "$ci_wf" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

gh workflow run "${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"

```bash

gh workflow run machine-sm.yml -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -f dryRun=false

`machine-sm.yml`'s `workflow_dispatch` input `dryRun` **defaults to `true`** (and `sm_kicker_test.dart` pins that default), so the factory dispatches a **dry tick**: it logs its plan and performs no action. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: CI-active dedup is dead — the pack matches runs by display name, but receives a file name**

Verified against `factory-sm-kicker.yml@01a45d24`: the head-completeness leg does

```bash
--jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\" and (...status...))] | length"
```

with `ci_wf='ci.yml'` (this stub's `ciWorkflow` input). But GitHub's `workflow_runs[].name` is the workflow's **display name** — `ci.yml` declares `name: CI` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:10`), so `.name` is `"CI"`, never `"ci.yml"`. The old local code matched `.name == "CI"` for exactly this reason.

Consequences, both behavior regressions vs. the deleted code:

1. `"CI already active on <sha> — skip"` never matches → every kicker tick (cron :13/:43 **plus every push on any PR branch**) re-dispatches `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref b` on a codeless head while CI is already queued/running on it → duplicate CI runs, queue pressure.
2. The 45-second grace re-check ("CI appeared during grace window") compares the same way → never sees CI → the dedup the grace window exists for is dead.

**Fix path**: in the pack, match on `.path == ".github/workflows/$ci_wf"` (stable, no extra input needed) or take the display name as a separate input; then flip this pin. Not merge-blocking on its own (the required-contexts check still bounds the duplicates once contexts land), but it contradicts the PR's parity claim and wastes real runner minutes on an active repo.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `github.token` mapped through the reusable call's `secrets` — this repo's own live evidence says it arrives empty**

`machine-sm.yml` records the outcome of a live bisect on this exact pattern:

> NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.

That stub deliberately routes `${{ github.token }}` through an **input** (`silent-token`), not the secrets block. This PR maps `githubToken: ${{ github.token }}` straight into `secrets`, which `factory-sm-kicker.yml` then uses as `GH_TOKEN` for every `gh api`/`gh workflow run` call. If the quirk reproduces here, **both** kicker legs 401 on every tick — the watchdog dies silently (no SM rescue, no CI on codeless heads, PRs stuck with zero required contexts) and nothing in the stub surfaces the failure.

The pack's header example does show this exact mapping (dmtools-agents #585 presumably tested it), so the two repos' live evidence currently disagrees. Before merge, please:

1. re-verify on the first scheduled/dispatch run of this stub that the legs authenticate (a green run log with "SM alive" / a CI dispatch, not 401s), or cite that evidence from #585;
2. if empty, either extend the factory to accept the token as an input (the `machine-sm` pattern) or use `secrets: inherit`, and flip the pin.

The blast radius if it breaks is the entire PR-unblocking flow this watchdog exists to keep alive — worth the explicit check rather than discovering it during the next stuck PR.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: pin skew vs. the lockstep invariant — and the new stub escapes the guard that enforces it**

Two related problems:

1. **Pin skew.** This stub pins `@01a45d24` while `machine-sm.yml`, `machine-merge.yml` and `ai-teammate.yml` all pin `@cee5996`. The invariant in `test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart` is explicit: *"all THREE stubs pin the SAME ref … a stale merge stub silently misses pack fixes"* (added after live skew, pr-1076/#568). The kicker now executes pack code that includes #577–#584, while the SM leg it dispatches still runs `cee5996` — any loop fix in #580–#584 that spans kicker↔SM behavior is half-applied, silently. Flipping all four stubs to the same SHA in one wave is the established remedy.

2. **Guard escape.** The same test file says: *"New stubs MUST be added here: the lockstep, factory_ref-echo and secrets checks below iterate this map, so an unlisted stub escapes all three."* `sm-kicker.yml` is a new factory stub (the 4th) and is **not** in the `stubs` map, so no lockstep, pin-format, or secrets check covers it — this PR is exactly how an unlisted stub drifts. (Verified: the test still passes on this branch, which proves the gap.)

**Fix in this PR**: add `'sm-kicker.yml': (kicker, 'factory-sm-kicker.yml')` to the `stubs` map (the `factory_ref`-echo check needs a skip-or-field decision — this factory workflow declares no `factory_ref` input, unlike the other three) and either flip the other three pins to `01a45d24` or document in the map why the kicker legitimately pins a different snapshot. Note the strict-secrets check will also need adapting: this stub maps `githubToken`, not `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN`.

blocks.text:
# SM kicker factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# A tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost) ported from
# flutter_agent_harness `.github/workflows/sm-kicker.yml` so every machine
# repo gets it from the pack instead of keeping a drifting local copy.
#
# Why it exists: machine repos run dispatch-only CI (ci.yml `on.push` fires
# nothing on PR heads) and the Machine SM is the sole trigger. Two gaps
# leave a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick
#      and die.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet the
#      strict `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on
#      the new head SHA. The SM's validate-fresh/armed rules don't count
#      a no-code rebase as "validation due", so the contexts never appear.
#      Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents, 0 files
#      vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check contexts
#      NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on that head.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).
#
# Caller stub (flutter_agent_harness example):
#   name: SM kicker
#   on:
#     push: {branches-ignore: [main]}
#     schedule: [{cron: '13,43 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch:
#   permissions: {actions: write, contents: read, pull-requests: read, checks: read}
#   concurrency:
#     # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911, 2026-09-25):
#     # a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker for every
#     # other branch, stamping CANCELLED check-runs on random heads. The
#     # kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let them queue.
#     group: sm-kicker
#     cancel-in-progress: false
#   jobs:
#     kicker:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml            # this repo's SM stub name
#         ciWorkflow: ci.yml                    # this repo's CI entrypoint
#         requiredContexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
#   # No secrets needed: the kicker reads github.token directly (it resolves
#   # to the CALLER's token inside a reusable workflow).
#   # epam/dmtools-dart example overrides:
#   #   smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml, ciWorkflow: quality.yml
#   #   requiredContexts: 'agents-suite,static,gate'
#
# Concurrency note: the group lives in the CALLER's job definition (GitHub
# attaches job-level concurrency to the reusable job) — keep the
# no-cancel-in-progress discipline from fa #911 there.

name: 'Factory · SM kicker'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label for the watchdog jobs (seconds-cheap; hosted is fine)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      smWorkflow:
        description: "File name of this repo's Machine SM stub to liveness-kick"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ciWorkflow:
        description: "File name of this repo's CI entrypoint to dispatch on codeless heads"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      requiredContexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check-run names guarding PR mergeability'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
      graceSeconds:
        description: 'Re-check window before dispatching CI (a dispatch may be in flight from the SM chain)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '45'
    secrets: {}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    env:
      # github.token resolves to the CALLER's token inside a reusable
      # workflow — no secret plumbing needed for reads + same-repo dispatch.
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            # dryRun=false is LOAD-BEARING: the SM stub's workflow_dispatch
            # input defaults to true, and a flagless dispatch silently no-ops
            # (live incident 2026-09-29 21:14-21:24Z, fa guard #1092).
            gh workflow run "${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -f dryRun=false
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    env:
      # github.token resolves to the CALLER's token inside a reusable
      # workflow — no secret plumbing needed for reads + same-repo dispatch.
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          req='${{ inputs.requiredContexts }}'
          ci_wf='${{ inputs.ciWorkflow }}'
          grace='${{ inputs.graceSeconds }}'
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\" and (.status == \"in_progress\" or .status == \"queued\" or .status == \"waiting\" or .status == \"pending\"))] | length")
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '[.check_runs[].name] | join("\n")' | grep -Fxc -f <(printf '%s\n' "${req//,//$'\n'}") || true)
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep "$grace"
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\")] | length")
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run "$ci_wf" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments.
