blocks.text:
# SM kicker factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# A tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost) ported from
# flutter_agent_harness `.github/workflows/sm-kicker.yml` so every machine
# repo gets it from the pack instead of keeping a drifting local copy.
#
# Why it exists: machine repos run dispatch-only CI (ci.yml `on.push` fires
# nothing on PR heads) and the Machine SM is the sole trigger. Two gaps
# leave a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick
#      and die.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet the
#      strict `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on
#      the new head SHA. The SM's validate-fresh/armed rules don't count
#      a no-code rebase as "validation due", so the contexts never appear.
#      Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents, 0 files
#      vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check contexts
#      NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on that head.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).
#
# Caller stub (flutter_agent_harness example):
#   name: SM kicker
#   on:
#     push: {branches-ignore: [main]}
#     schedule: [{cron: '13,43 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch:
#   permissions: {actions: write, contents: read, pull-requests: read, checks: read}
#   concurrency:
#     # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911, 2026-09-25):
#     # a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker for every
#     # other branch, stamping CANCELLED check-runs on random heads. The
#     # kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let them queue.
#     group: sm-kicker
#     cancel-in-progress: false
#   jobs:
#     kicker:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml            # this repo's SM stub name
#         ciWorkflow: ci.yml                    # this repo's CI entrypoint
#         requiredContexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
#   # No secrets needed: the kicker reads github.token directly (it resolves
#   # to the CALLER's token inside a reusable workflow).
#   # epam/dmtools-dart example overrides:
#   #   smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml, ciWorkflow: quality.yml
#   #   requiredContexts: 'agents-suite,static,gate'
#
# Concurrency note: the group lives in the CALLER's job definition (GitHub
# attaches job-level concurrency to the reusable job) — keep the
# no-cancel-in-progress discipline from fa #911 there.

name: 'Factory · SM kicker'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label for the watchdog jobs (seconds-cheap; hosted is fine)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      smWorkflow:
        description: "File name of this repo's Machine SM stub to liveness-kick"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ciWorkflow:
        description: "File name of this repo's CI entrypoint to dispatch on codeless heads"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      requiredContexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check-run names guarding PR mergeability'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
      graceSeconds:
        description: 'Re-check window before dispatching CI (a dispatch may be in flight from the SM chain)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '45'
    secrets: {}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    env:
      # github.token resolves to the CALLER's token inside a reusable
      # workflow — no secret plumbing needed for reads + same-repo dispatch.
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            # dryRun=false is LOAD-BEARING: the SM stub's workflow_dispatch
            # input defaults to true, and a flagless dispatch silently no-ops
            # (live incident 2026-09-29 21:14-21:24Z, fa guard #1092).
            gh workflow run "${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -f dryRun=false
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    env:
      # github.token resolves to the CALLER's token inside a reusable
      # workflow — no secret plumbing needed for reads + same-repo dispatch.
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          req='${{ inputs.requiredContexts }}'
          ci_wf='${{ inputs.ciWorkflow }}'
          grace='${{ inputs.graceSeconds }}'
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\" and (.status == \"in_progress\" or .status == \"queued\" or .status == \"waiting\" or .status == \"pending\"))] | length")
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '[.check_runs[].name] | join("\n")' | grep -Fxc -f <(printf '%s\n' "${req//,//$'\n'}") || true)
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep "$grace"
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\")] | length")
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run "$ci_wf" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

re-read changed files,

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # SM kicker — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml
# (this repo carries only triggers + concurrency + this call — no logic to drift).
# Ported from the previous local copy (fa history: two-job watchdog,
# #911 concurrency diagnosis).
#
# Why it exists: this repo's CI is dispatch-only (ci.yml `on.push` fires
# nothing on PR heads) and the Machine SM is the sole trigger:
#   1. sm-liveness — SM idle → dispatch one tick;
#   2. head-completeness — codeless merge heads (2 parents, 0 files) with
#      zero required contexts get a CI dispatch (strict up-to-date).
#
# Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents main @01a45d24a071536a9f39603c2571f2e10f84a0b1 — ships the kicker
# together with the #577-#584 loop fixes (lockstep with machine-sm /
# machine-merge / ai-teammate stubs' pin wave).

name: SM kicker

run-name: 🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: machine-sm.yml / ci.yml
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911 diagnosis, 2026-09-25):
  # a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker for every
  # other branch, leaving sm-liveness/head-completeness check-runs stamped
  # CANCELLED on random heads ("Cancelled after 6s") and polluting PR
  # check rolls repo-wide. The kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs —
  # let them queue instead of cancelling; a bounded backlog is harmless.
  group: sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@01a45d24a071536a9f39603c2571f2e10f84a0b1
    with:
      smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml
      ciWorkflow: ci.yml
      requiredContexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
      graceSeconds: '45'
    secrets:
      githubToken: ${{ github.token }}

The repo is at the PR branch. Now let me:
1. Read AGENTS.md for conventions
2. Look at the other factory stubs (machine-sm.yml, machine-merge.yml, ai-teammate.yml) to compare conventions — especially how they pass secrets and pin SHAs.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

The AGENTS.md is huge. It's mostly about the Dart project itself. Let me search for anything about workflows/CI conventions in AGENTS.md to understand if there are specific patterns. But it's a big file. Let me focus on what matters for this review: the workflow file conventions. Let me look at other factory stubs to compare conventions (machine-sm.yml, machine-merge.yml, ai-teammate.yml).

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents main @cee599626b0ee12111dc8fb27ece83daebd9ae6e — ships:
    # #579 (conflict-rework: PR-anchored dispatch when no OPEN linked
    # issue — DIRTY machines PRs no longer dead-letter on closed issues),
    # #577/#578 (mutexExcludeSelf by fact of holding: a self-holding
    # candidate IS the holder — two approved ai_validating arms no longer
    # block each other into a total queue freeze; live fa #1068+#1088
    # 2026-09-30, ~40 min deadlock), #576 (review-machine-unlinked: a
    # MACHINE-authored validated PR with no OPEN linked issue gets its
    # one-time review — fixes the validated-forever starvation, live fa
    # #1068 19h / #1071 / #1075), #573 (every pack release is a
    # self-contained snapshot), #574 (DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY passed into
    # the agent run env), #572 (review-stale-verdict-unchecked: a
    # validated+reviewed PR whose head lost its checks gets a re-REVIEW
    # first; final validation stays in validate-armed), #571 (factory
    # teammate leg self-heals a broken dmtools install), #570 (SM
    # workflow budget 1 -> 3), #569 (rework: a fatal CLI failure is no
    # longer announced as "Rework Complete"),
    # #568 (mergeBot workspace/repository args), #566 (pack-registry
    # runner overrides).
    # Flip in lockstep with ai-teammate.yml — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@cee599626b0ee12111dc8fb27ece83daebd9ae6e
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: cee599626b0ee12111dc8fb27ece83daebd9ae6e
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

Very interesting. Key findings so far:

1. **Critical pattern inconsistency**: The repo's convention for `github.token` passing to the factory is documented in machine-sm.yml:

   > NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.

   So the new sm-kicker stub passes `secrets: githubToken: ${{ github.token }}`. Per the live-verified experience in machine-sm.yml, `${{ github.token }}` mapped through a reusable call's secrets block arrives EMPTY at the callee. If factory-sm-kicker.yml declares a `githubToken` secret and uses it for `gh api` calls, the kicker would fail (or partially fail — silently, since these are watchdog jobs).

   However — wait, this needs care. The note says "GitHub delivers an empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets (live-verified)". Actually, in general GitHub DOES pass github.token through secrets blocks of reusable workflows... Actually the documented behavior: `github.token` in the caller's context is available; when passed into a reusable workflow via secrets, the callee receives... Let me think. There are known GitHub quirks: In reusable workflows, `secrets: inherit` passes github.token fine. Explicit mapping `SECRET: ${{ github.token }}` — there are reports that this works. But the repo's own live-verified experience says it arrived empty. blocks.text:
# SM kicker factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# A tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost) ported from
# flutter_agent_harness `.github/workflows/sm-kicker.yml` so every machine
# repo gets it from the pack instead of keeping a drifting local copy.
#
# Why it exists: machine repos run dispatch-only CI (ci.yml `on.push` fires
# nothing on PR heads) and the Machine SM is the sole trigger. Two gaps
# leave a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick
#      and die.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet the
#      strict `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on
#      the new head SHA. The SM's validate-fresh/armed rules don't count
#      a no-code rebase as "validation due", so the contexts never appear.
#      Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents, 0 files
#      vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check contexts
#      NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on that head.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).
#
# Caller stub (flutter_agent_harness example):
#   name: SM kicker
#   on:
#     push: {branches-ignore: [main]}
#     schedule: [{cron: '13,43 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch:
#   permissions: {actions: write, contents: read, pull-requests: read, checks: read}
#   concurrency:
#     # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911, 2026-09-25):
#     # a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker for every
#     # other branch, stamping CANCELLED check-runs on random heads. The
#     # kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let them queue.
#     group: sm-kicker
#     cancel-in-progress: false
#   jobs:
#     kicker:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml            # this repo's SM stub name
#         ciWorkflow: ci.yml                    # this repo's CI entrypoint
#         requiredContexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
#       secrets:
#         githubToken: ${{ github.token }}
#   # epam/dmtools-dart example overrides:
#   #   smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml, ciWorkflow: quality.yml
#   #   requiredContexts: 'agents-suite,static,gate'
#
# Concurrency note: the group lives in the CALLER's job definition (GitHub
# attaches job-level concurrency to the reusable job) — keep the
# no-cancel-in-progress discipline from fa #911 there.

name: 'Factory · SM kicker'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label for the watchdog jobs (seconds-cheap; hosted is fine)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      smWorkflow:
        description: "File name of this repo's Machine SM stub to liveness-kick"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ciWorkflow:
        description: "File name of this repo's CI entrypoint to dispatch on codeless heads"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      requiredContexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check-run names guarding PR mergeability'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
      graceSeconds:
        description: 'Re-check window before dispatching CI (a dispatch may be in flight from the SM chain)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '45'
    secrets:
      githubToken:
        description: "Caller's token (github.token suffices: reads + same-repo workflow dispatch)"

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.githubToken }}
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            gh workflow run "${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.githubToken }}
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          req='${{ inputs.requiredContexts }}'
          ci_wf='${{ inputs.ciWorkflow }}'
          grace='${{ inputs.graceSeconds }}'
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\" and (.status == \"in_progress\" or .status == \"queued\" or .status == \"waiting\" or .status == \"pending\"))] | length")
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '[.check_runs[].name] | join("\n")' | grep -Fxc -f <(printf '%s\n' "${req//,//$'\n'}") || true)
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep "$grace"
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\")] | length")
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run "$ci_wf" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

blocks.text:
# SM kicker factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# A tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost) ported from
# flutter_agent_harness `.github/workflows/sm-kicker.yml` so every machine
# repo gets it from the pack instead of keeping a drifting local copy.
#
# Why it exists: machine repos run dispatch-only CI (ci.yml `on.push` fires
# nothing on PR heads) and the Machine SM is the sole trigger. Two gaps
# leave a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick
#      and die.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet the
#      strict `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on
#      the new head SHA. The SM's validate-fresh/armed rules don't count
#      a no-code rebase as "validation due", so the contexts never appear.
#      Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents, 0 files
#      vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check contexts
#      NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on that head.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).
#
# Caller stub (flutter_agent_harness example):
#   name: SM kicker
#   on:
#     push: {branches-ignore: [main]}
#     schedule: [{cron: '13,43 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch:
#   permissions: {actions: write, contents: read, pull-requests: read, checks: read}
#   concurrency:
#     # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911, 2026-09-25):
#     # a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker for every
#     # other branch, stamping CANCELLED check-runs on random heads. The
#     # kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let them queue.
#     group: sm-kicker
#     cancel-in-progress: false
#   jobs:
#     kicker:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml            # this repo's SM stub name
#         ciWorkflow: ci.yml                    # this repo's CI entrypoint
#         requiredContexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
#   # No secrets needed: the kicker reads github.token directly (it resolves
#   # to the CALLER's token inside a reusable workflow).
#   # epam/dmtools-dart example overrides:
#   #   smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml, ciWorkflow: quality.yml
#   #   requiredContexts: 'agents-suite,static,gate'
#
# Concurrency note: the group lives in the CALLER's job definition (GitHub
# attaches job-level concurrency to the reusable job) — keep the
# no-cancel-in-progress discipline from fa #911 there.

name: 'Factory · SM kicker'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label for the watchdog jobs (seconds-cheap; hosted is fine)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      smWorkflow:
        description: "File name of this repo's Machine SM stub to liveness-kick"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ciWorkflow:
        description: "File name of this repo's CI entrypoint to dispatch on codeless heads"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      requiredContexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check-run names guarding PR mergeability'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
      graceSeconds:
        description: 'Re-check window before dispatching CI (a dispatch may be in flight from the SM chain)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '45'
    secrets: {}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    env:
      # github.token resolves to the CALLER's token inside a reusable
      # workflow — no secret plumbing needed for reads + same-repo dispatch.
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            # dryRun=false is LOAD-BEARING: the SM stub's workflow_dispatch
            # input defaults to true, and a flagless dispatch silently no-ops
            # (live incident 2026-09-29 21:14-21:24Z, fa guard #1092).
            gh workflow run "${{ inputs.smWorkflow }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -f dryRun=false
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    env:
      # github.token resolves to the CALLER's token inside a reusable
      # workflow — no secret plumbing needed for reads + same-repo dispatch.
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          req='${{ inputs.requiredContexts }}'
          ci_wf='${{ inputs.ciWorkflow }}'
          grace='${{ inputs.graceSeconds }}'
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\" and (.status == \"in_progress\" or .status == \"queued\" or .status == \"waiting\" or .status == \"pending\"))] | length")
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '[.check_runs[].name] | join("\n")' | grep -Fxc -f <(printf '%s\n' "${req//,//$'\n'}") || true)
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep "$grace"
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\")] | length")
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run "$ci_wf" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (carried over from round 1, Thread 8 — still present in `@a5e377d`): the pack matches CI runs by display name, but receives a file name**

Round 1 fixed #586 (`dryRun=false`) and #587 (inline token) — thank you, both verified in the pack source. The third finding is still open: `factory-sm-kicker.yml@a5e377d9aa417d7537efd452a0dba06454132dec` head-completeness leg still does

```bash
--jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == \"$ci_wf\" and (...status...))] | length"
```

with `ci_wf='ci.yml'`. GitHub's `workflow_runs[].name` is the workflow's **display name** — `ci.yml` declares `name: CI` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:10`), so `.name` is `"CI"`, never `"ci.yml"`. The pre-port local code matched `.name == "CI"` for exactly this reason.

Consequences (both regressions vs. the deleted code, against the PR's parity claim):

1. `"CI already active on <sha> — skip"` never matches → every kicker trigger (cron :13/:43 **plus every push on any PR branch**) re-dispatches `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref b` on a codeless head while CI is already queued/running on it → duplicate CI runs on a repo with heavy CI.
2. The grace re-check ("CI appeared during grace window") compares the same way → the 45-second dedup window is dead.

**Fix path** (pack-side, then flip this pin): match on `.path == ".github/workflows/$ci_wf"` — stable, no extra input needed — or accept the display name as a second input. Optionally add a pack-side regression guard so the next port can't reintroduce it (the #1092 pattern).

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# SM kicker — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml
# (this repo carries only triggers + concurrency + this call — no logic to drift).
# Ported from the previous local copy (fa history: two-job watchdog,
# #911 concurrency diagnosis).
#
# Why it exists: this repo's CI is dispatch-only (ci.yml `on.push` fires
# nothing on PR heads) and the Machine SM is the sole trigger:
#   1. sm-liveness — SM idle → dispatch one tick;
#   2. head-completeness — codeless merge heads (2 parents, 0 files) with
#      zero required contexts get a CI dispatch (strict up-to-date).
#
# Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents main @01a45d24a071536a9f39603c2571f2e10f84a0b1 — ships the kicker
# together with the #577-#584 loop fixes (lockstep with machine-sm /
# machine-merge / ai-teammate stubs' pin wave).

name: SM kicker

run-name: 🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: machine-sm.yml / ci.yml
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911 diagnosis, 2026-09-25):
  # a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker for every
  # other branch, leaving sm-liveness/head-completeness check-runs stamped
  # CANCELLED on random heads ("Cancelled after 6s") and polluting PR
  # check rolls repo-wide. The kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs —
  # let them queue instead of cancelling; a bounded backlog is harmless.
  group: sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@01a45d24a071536a9f39603c2571f2e10f84a0b1
    with:
      smWorkflow: machine-sm.yml
      ciWorkflow: ci.yml
      requiredContexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
      graceSeconds: '45'
    secrets:
      githubToken: ${{ github.token }}

1. Read AGENTS.md for conventions
2. Look at the other factory stubs (machine-sm.yml, machine-merge.yml, ai-teammate.yml) to compare conventions — especially how they pass secrets and pin SHAs.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

The AGENTS.md is huge. It's mostly about the Dart project itself. Let me search for anything about workflows/CI conventions in AGENTS.md to understand if there are specific patterns. But it's a big file. Let me focus on what matters for this review: the workflow file conventions. Let me look at other factory stubs to compare conventions (machine-sm.yml, machine-merge.yml, ai-teammate.yml).
